description: chain_walk (line 747) applies BasicConstraints and KeyUsage checks for all i > 0. chain[chain.len()-1] is the last certificate in the chain, which is issued by a trust anchor. If chain.len() >= 3, chain[chain.len()-1] is an intermediate and correctly gets CA checks. But chain[chain.len()-1] is also the cert whose signature is verified against the anchor SPKI — it is NOT the anchor itself. For a 2-cert chain [leaf, intermediate], i=1 gets CA checks (correct). For a 1-cert chain [leaf], i=0 and the check is skipped (correct, leaf is not an intermediate). However: for a 1-cert self-signed chain where the cert IS a CA, i=0 so BasicConstraints/KeyUsage are NOT checked. A self-signed non-CA leaf used as the only chain element will pass all intermediate checks because i=0 is excluded. This is correct behavior (RFC 5280 does not require the EE to be a CA) but it means a trust anchor that is itself presented as chain[0] without any intermediates bypasses ALL CA property checks. Document this explicitly.
title: chain_walk checks intermediate CA constraints at i>0 but trust anchor is at i=chain.len()-1
